taskVersion.name: ves-synthetic-a-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station T-05, survey area T. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 1320.7 | 0.60 | 0.60
2 | 719.2 | 0.46 | 1.06
3 | 872.7 | 0.61 | 1.67
4 | 340.7 | 0.38 | 2.05
5 | 4088.9 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as HKH-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station T-05, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Site Report – Station T-05, Survey Area T**

The interpreted resistivity model shows five layers. Resistivity decreases from 1320.7 Ω·m (Layer 1) to 719.2 Ω·m (Layer 2), rises to 872.7 Ω·m (Layer 3), drops sharply to 340.7 Ω·m (Layer 4), then increases markedly to 4088.9 Ω·m (Layer 5). Total depth of the layered sequence (to base of Layer 4) is 2.05 m, with Layer 5 acting as the resistive basement.

Checking the curve-type notation: Layers 1-2-3 give H (r1>r2<r3), Layers 2-3-4 give K (r2<r3... wait check: r2<r3>r4) = K, Layers 3-4-5 give H (r3>r4<r5). This yields HKH, consistent with the filed classification.

The HKH-type curve is confirmed by the resistivity sequence, indicating alternating high-low-high-low-high resistivity layering typical of mixed lithological contrasts at this site.

{"curve_type_stated": "HKH", "label_issue_flagged": false}
